    AI Overview
    Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged, long-term investment accounts for U.S. citizen children under 18, launched via the 2025 "One Big Beautiful Bill". Launching July 4, 2026, they allow $5,000 in annual contributions, with a $1,000 government seed deposit for children born 2025–2028, managed by adults until age 18. 
    Key Details for Trump Accounts (530A): 
    • Eligibility & Seed Money: All U.S. citizen children under 18 with a Social Security number are eligible. A $1,000 federal pilot contribution is available for children born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028.
    • How to Open: Parents/guardians can sign up on TrumpAccounts.gov or by filing IRS Form 4547
      with their 2025 tax return.
    • Contributions: Parents, relatives, or employers can contribute up to $5,000 per child, per year (indexed for inflation in 2028).
    • Tax Treatment: Earnings grow tax-deferred (similar to an IRA) until withdrawal, with the account owned by the child.
    • Purpose: Designed for long-term growth, which can be used for future milestones like education or home purchases. 
    As of April 2026, about 5 million children have been registered for the program.

    People also ask
    How can I get a Trump Account for my child?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    To open a Trump Account for a child, parents or legal guardians must file IRS Form 4547 (starting mid-2026) or use the online portal at trumpaccounts.gov. The accounts allow up to
    in annual contributions for U.S. citizen children under 18. A
    pilot seed contribution is available for children born between 2025–2028. 
    Steps to Open a Trump Account 
    1. Verify Eligibility: The child must be under 18 years old and have a valid Social Security number. For the
      pilot program, the child must be a U.S. citizen born between 2025–2028.
    2. File IRS Form 4547: Submit Form 4547, "Trump Account Election(s)," which can be done starting in mid-2026.
      • With Taxes:
        Include the form with your 2025 tax return.
      • Online Portal: Use the online submission portal.
    3. Activate Account: Beginning in May 2026, the Treasury Department or its agent will send information to complete the account setup and authentication process.
    4. Wait for Contributions: Contributions cannot be made until after July 4, 2026. 
    Key Details 
    • Account Owner: The child is the owner of the account.
    • Management: Parents, guardians, or adult relatives can open the account.
    • Funding: Anyone can contribute, up to a total of
      per child annually.
    • Access: Funds cannot be withdrawn until the child reaches age 18.
    • Transfer: Initial accounts are held with a Treasury-designated agent but can be transferred to personal brokerages later.
